court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
facts_of_case: Petitioner filed petition for maintenance under Section 125 Cr.PC; trial court awarded Rs.7,000/-p.m. to respondent and Rs.10,000/-p.m. towards maintenance; petitioner is before this Court seeking to set aside the order.

legal_principles.principle: A spouse who leaves the matrimonial home voluntarily without any valid reasons is not entitled to claim maintenance.
legal_principles.held: The wife left the matrimonial home voluntarily on her own without any valid reasons and not filed the counter in the petition for restitution of conjugal rights for a period of more than two years and refused to live together with the petitioner shows that the first respondent/wife is not entitled to claim any maintenance under Section 125(4) Cr.PC.

legal_principles.principle: A person who takes effective steps to take back their spouse and child by invoking the provisions under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act is not neglecting or refusing to maintain them.
legal_principles.held: The revision petitioner has taken effective steps to take back the wife and child by invoking the provisions under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act and Section 7 of the Guardians and Wards Act.

outcome.final_order: The order of the Magistrate is set aside.

keywords: Latin maxim: Nemo dat quod non habet
use_for_drafting: representing clients in family law disputes
